source_refs.note: Turbulent Flow: a main subheading of 5.8 Steady, non-viscous and ideal fluid, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 104-104.

blocks.text: The irregular or unsteady flow of the fluid is called turbulent flow.
bold: The irregular or unsteady flow of the fluid is called turbulent flow.

blocks.text: Above a certain velocity of the fluid flow, the motion of the fluid becomes unsteady and irregular. Under this condition, the velocity of the fluid changes abruptly as shown in the Fig. 5.13. In this case, the exact path of the particles cannot be considered.

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text:
Formula One racing cars have a streamlined design.
Dolphins have streamlined bodies to assist their movement in water.

blocks.alt: A Formula One racing car seen from the side, speeding to the right on a track between grass verges: a long, low green-and-blue body with a pointed nose, a front wing and a tall rear wing, the driver in a helmet in the open cockpit, and large black tyres.
blocks.caption: Formula One racing cars have a streamlined design (original drawing after the photograph printed in the textbook).

blocks.alt: Two grey dolphins swimming side by side through deep blue water, heading down to the right, with smooth tapering bodies, paler bellies, curved dorsal fins, flippers and tail flukes.
blocks.caption: Dolphins have streamlined bodies to assist their movement in water (original drawing after the photograph printed in the textbook).

blocks.text: If two streamlines cross each other, then the particles will go in one or in the other directions and flow will not be a steady flow. Such a flow is a turbulent flow. When the flow is unsteady or turbulent, there are eddies and whirlpools in the motion and the paths of the particles are continuously changing.
